text:
Maya Patel: Hey team — Customer ACME (ticket #765432) reports a sudden spike of 502/504s and a handful of 5xx streaming connection resets over the last hour. They say it happens during bursts (~600 concurrent requests) and the SDK ends up in a retry loop causing duplicate billing. Repro steps attached below.

Maya Patel: Repro steps from customer:
1) SDK v1.4.2, nodejs, default retry config.
2) Region: eu-west-1, endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
3) Run 600 concurrent streaming requests for ~30s. ~3-5% fail with 502/504 and then sdk retries 3x and bills.

Maya Patel: They included logs:
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] requestId=abcd1234 status=200 latency=120ms
[2026-03-15T09:12:05Z] requestId=abcd5678 status=502 upstream=ingress-proxy error="connection reset by peer"
[2026-03-15T09:12:05Z] sdk_retry requestId=abcd5678 attempt=1
[2026-03-15T09:12:06Z] requestId=abcd5678 status=504 upstream=edge timeouts=idle_conn
```

Maya Patel: Customer wants a root cause and either a fix or recommended mitigation asap. They're worried about billing chargebacks.

Ethan Cole: Thanks — pinging eng-runtime and eng-sre. @Devon can you take a look at ingress backpressure traces for that timeframe? I see a small p95 latency bump in metrics around 09:12UTC.

Devon Kim: On it. Can you drop the full request headers and SDK config? curious about keepalive and http2 concurrency.

Maya Patel: From customer:
```
SDK: @redwood/sdk-node v1.4.2
Node: 18.17
Concurrency: 600 parallel streams
Timeouts: default (no override)
Connection: http2 enabled, keepalive: default
Auth: short-lived bearer tokens rotated every 5 min (we use our k8s sidecar to refresh)
```

Lena Ortiz: Billing bot — tagging for visibility. Billing Bot: please advise on duplicate charges if SDK retries are billed.

Billing Bot: @Lena Ortiz confirmed — retried requests that result in separate successful tokens are billable per usual. We can work with finance on customer credits but need engineering root cause first.

Devon Kim: Quick initial notes: ingress logs show many upstream resets from the proxy layer around that minute. Not obvious auth failures. Hoping to correlate with connection churn on the edge pool. Can we get flow logs for the host nodes?

Ethan Cole: I pulled edge node connection counts — there was a GC spike on node eu-edge-12 around 09:11 that coincides with a short pause in accepting new streams. Could be a runtimeside stall under heavy concurrency.

Devon Kim: Interesting — GC pause plus http2 stream window pressure could cause upstream to reset connections. If SDK doesn't backoff properly on streaming resets, it'll retry and re-open streams, amplifying load.

Maya Patel: Customer reported the SDK was doing an immediate retry with same concurrency settings — leads to retry storm. They asked if we can suggest SDK config changes while we investigate.

Ethan Cole: Immediate mitigation suggestions for customer:
- Reduce parallel streaming concurrency to 200-300 for now.
- Set SDK backoff policy: exponential with jitter, base 200ms, max 5s, and max attempts 3.
- Prefer non-streaming batch generation for heavy bursts if possible.
- Pin to region-specific endpoint: eu-west-1 to avoid cross-region routing.

Devon Kim: Also: temporary server-side mitigation we can enable quickly — set per-edge connection concurrent stream caps lower for the customer (rate-limit token) and enable early 429 on overload so SDK backoffs instead of connection resets. I can push a canary config.

Maya Patel: Customer OK with mitigation if it prevents duplicate charges. Please coordinate.

Ethan Cole: @deploy-bot scheduling a canary config change to edge pool for customer token — small ramp, 5% traffic first.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary-edge-config/customer-765432 at 2026-03-15T09:28:40Z by Ethan Cole

Devon Kim: While canary warms, I'm going to pull heap/GC traces from the runtime instances that served the customer. If we see large allocations or improper connection handling under http2, we'll correlate to SDK behavior.

Maya Patel: Customer asked for an FAQ response they can send internally. Drafting a short note once we have confirmation of mitigation and a timeline.

Ethan Cole: Update: canary shows reduced connection resets for the sample traffic at 09:30. Edge logs: resets down from 3.2% -> 0.4% for the canary cohort. Continuing to monitor for 30m.

Billing Bot: Flagging for billing ops — keep me posted if customer requests credits. Current policy requires engineering confirmation of system fault contributing to retries.

Devon Kim: Runtime traces show two interesting things: 1) a small hot object allocation during stream handshake causing a few ms pause; 2) http2 GO runtime had a goroutine stall due to a lock contention path in connection reuse. I'll open a runtime bug and a patch to reduce allocation in the handshake. Patch impacts kernel APIs in: runtime/transport.go

Devon Kim: Patch notes (working):
```
- reduce allocations in stream handshake
- improve reuse path to avoid lock on fast path
- add metrics around active http2 streams per connection
```

Ethan Cole: Good. Plan: 1) keep canary config for the customer for 24h 2) backport runtime patch to a hotfix build and roll to edge pool with a staged deploy 3) recommend customer SDK backoff config and concurrency cap.

Maya Patel: I'll send customer the draft: short summary + recommended SDK settings + what we changed (canary + next steps) + offer of billing review after we confirm less than 1% retries. Draft below:

"ACME team — update: We observed connection resets triggered by edge overload + a runtime lock contention under very high concurrent streaming. We've enabled a targeted canary rate-limit for your token to reduce resets and deployed a runtime hotfix into canary. Recommended immediate actions on your side: reduce parallel streaming to 250 and set SDK backoff to exponential with jitter (base=200ms, max=5s, attempts=3). We'll monitor for 24h and follow up with billing reconciliation if system behavior caused retries. — Maya (Support)"

Maya Patel: Customer responded: "OK, reducing concurrency now. appreciate the quick help."

Ethan Cole: Will open a postmortem stub and link to this thread. Assigning owner: Devon for root cause and patch rollout.

Devon Kim: Created internal issue INF-1209 and pushed initial runtime branch for review. I'll schedule a hotfix rollout after code-review and perf tests.

Maya Patel: Thanks all. I'll keep this thread updated and post the customer-facing message once billing ops confirms next steps.

Ethan Cole: Nice work. Quick note for docs: we should add a KB on streaming concurrency best-practices and SDK backoff defaults.

Maya Patel: Agreed. I'll create a ticket in docs to draft KB.

deploy-bot: canary successful: edge-config/customer-765432 at 2026-03-15T09:31:12Z. Monitoring continuing.

Maya Patel: Closing loop for now. If anything flips back up I'll re-open the thread.

Devon Kim: I'll post updates in INF-1209 as we run the hotfix perf pass.

Billing Bot: Noted. Will wait for engineering confirmation before suggesting credits.

Maya Patel: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
